summary: United Launch Alliance has traced a recent Vulcan Centaur rocket anomaly—which resulted in the loss of 40 Amazon satellites—to an inadequate fuel supply to its first-stage engines, raising operational considerations for future military payloads. In commercial space developments, Finnish satellite operator ICEYE submitted a €2 billion ($2 billion) acquisition bid for Italian rocket manufacturer Avio, Inflection Space Systems booked its first orbital mission, and Flexell Space signed a memorandum of understanding with ALATYR to explore solar power solutions for orbital data centers. On the defense front, the U.S. Senate backed an expanded budget for the Space Force despite trimming overall Pentagon expenditure plans, while the Air Force executed a test launch of a Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile. In space science, observations confirmed by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope provided evidence of a first-of-its-kind stellar merger between a supergiant star and a smaller sun-like companion, and NASA's Voyager 1 probe reached a distance milestone of one light-day from Earth. In civil space policy and operations, NASA announced it will end science operations for its long-serving Terra satellite on Dec. 1, initiated the next Earth Science Decadal Survey, and launched a Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge for U.S. commercial partners. Readers should watch for NASA’s upcoming prelaunch coverage and scheduling updates for the Northrop Grumman CRS-25 resupply mission.
